applicability: Any two two-digit whole numbers with no zero digit — a zero digit is drawn as no lines at all, which the diagram cannot show. Draw each digit of the first number as that many parallel lines slanting one way, each digit of the second slanting the other, and count the crossings in each diagonal band: left to right the bands are hundreds, tens, units. Reading the three counts straight off as the digits of the answer is valid exactly when the units band and the tens band are each below 10. The leftmost band is not restricted — a count of 10 or more there simply spills into the thousands digit and still reads correctly.
carry_case: 23 × 22. The bands count 4 | 10 | 6, and '4 10 6' is not the answer: the tens band of 10 leaves 0 in the tens place and carries 1 into the hundreds, giving 506. Any pair whose tens band a1·b0 + a0·b1 reaches 10 breaks the straight read-off, and so does any pair whose units band a0·b0 reaches 10, e.g. 34 × 25. The leftmost band is the exception to the exception: 21 × 51 counts 10 | 7 | 1 and still reads off correctly as 1071.

steps.instruction: Draw each digit as that many lines, one number each way
Count the crossings in each diagonal band
Each band is the digit product a column would hold
A band of 10 or more carries left

operand_draw.unit: one decimal digit per draw, taken in order as a1, a0, b1, b0 — so a = 10·1 + 2 = 12 and b = 10·2 + 3 = 23
